Regional Partner Development Manager, Microsoft, Singapore. Job 200044526. Individual-contributor Sales role. 50-75% travel.
The Partner Development Manager (PDM) owns a portfolio of strategic partners and distributors in a region and is responsible for growing Microsoft's cloud business through them - driving cloud revenue, consumption, customer adds, and renewals across Solution Areas (AI, Security, Modern Work, Azure, Business Applications, Digital and App Innovation).
Core pillars:
1. Partner business leadership - executive relationships, partner business plans, business reviews.
2. Partner transformation - moving partners to cloud, AI and managed services and recurring revenue models, driving Microsoft designations and specializations and marketplace motions.
3. AI and Copilot growth - accelerating AI adoption, partner readiness, and packaged offerings.
4. Ecosystem orchestration - aligning PDMs, Partner Technology Strategists, Customer Success Unit, and Solution Area teams.
5. Performance management - pipeline management, forecasting, data-driven insights, corrective action planning, KPI performance management.
6. Strategic initiatives - regional programs and fiscal year planning.
Required: Bachelor's degree in Marketing, Business Operations, Computer Science or related field, plus 10 years of experience in partner management, sales, business development, or channel development in the technology industry, or equivalent.
Preferred: track record of growing business through ecosystem partners; executive influence and executive stakeholder management; cloud and enterprise technology depth; cross-functional leadership; cloud, AI, security and digital transformation experience; multi-country regional portfolio management; deep Microsoft partner ecosystem knowledge; MBA.
Skills: Account Management, Customer Success, Business Development, Change Management, Business, Management, go-to-market, GTM, managed services, recurring revenue, business transformation, capability development, market analysis, customer acquisition, renewals, consumption growth.
